result.title: CAST: Real-Time Motion Capture for Any Skeleton Topology
result.summary: This paper studies the problem of recovering motion from monocular video, even when the target skeleton topology differs from the subject observed in the video. Although previous methods have made efforts to resolve this problem, they remain vulnerable to joint-rotation errors that are coupled across the skeleton and can propagate along its kinematic hierarchy. To mitigate these errors, we present CAST, a topology-aware motion capture framework that combines learned local rotations with geometric correction guided by predicted global bone directions. Our observability analysis characterizes which rotational components can be constrained by outgoing bone directions. Guided by this analysis, GRACE uses reliability-gated alignment to correct composed orientations in parent-to-child order, leaving unconstrained components to the learned rotation predictor. The motion predictor and correction module are trained jointly with motion-derived supervision, using a frozen image encoder. Experiments under the TopoCap evaluation protocol show that the proposed framework improves motion recovery across different target topologies, including unseen structures. Reference-based cross-skeleton evaluation on a curated Mixamo benchmark and a user preference study further assess transfer to different target structures. A causal CAST-B variant achieves over 51 FPS on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, with timing covering image encoding and motion prediction. Code repository: https://github.com/fankewen/CAST.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CAST，一个拓扑感知的单目视频动作捕捉框架：当目标骨架拓扑与视频中主体不同时，用学到的局部旋转预测配合由预测全局骨骼方向引导的几何校正，并通过可观测性分析界定哪些旋转分量可由出射骨方向约束，再以可靠性门控按父到子顺序校正合成朝向；另提供因果流式变体与跨骨架基准评测。与 VLM 推理无关。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于动作捕捉这一远领域，但「可观测性分析界定哪些状态分量受观测约束、未约束部分交由学习预测器、以可靠性门控校正」的结构，可能为 LVR 中「哪些 latent 状态维度真正由视觉证据支撑、哪些需模型自行填补」以及证据筛选式更新提供类比性线索，需人工核查其可迁移性。
